content: Burow's solution is a pharmacological preparation composed of aluminum acetate dissolved in water. It was developed in the mid-1800s by Karl August Burow, an ophthalmologist. This solution possesses astringent and antibacterial properties, making it effective in the treatment of various dermatological conditions. These include insect bites, rashes caused by exposure to poison ivy and poison sumac, localized swelling, allergic reactions, and bruises. The solution is typically applied to the affected area using cold compresses to provide relief and promote healing. Burow's solution is available as an over-the-counter generic preparation. Additionally, Bayer produces a modified version of this preparation, which is marketed under the brand name Domeboro.
